test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which formula is used to calculate M3 (i.e. measure of money supply)?

options.text: M3 = M1 + Total deposits with post office
M3 = M1 + Total deposits with post office excluding National Saving Certificate
M3 = CU + DD + Net time deposits of commercial banks
M3 = M2 + Saving deposits with post office

solution:
The correct answer is __**M3 = CU + DD + Net time deposits of commercial banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Money supply -The total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time is called the money supply
 
• RBI publishes figures for four alternative measures of money

 supply, viz. M1, M2, M3 and M4. They are defined as follows
 
 
• M1 = CU(currency (notes plus coins) held by the public) + DD(net demand deposits held by commercial banks)
 
• M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
 
• M3 = M1 + Net time deposits of commercial banks
 
• M4 = M3 + Total deposits with Post Office savings organisations (excluding

 National Savings Certificates)
